constitutional_articles.title: Equality before law
constitutional_articles.description: Guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws to all persons. In criminal law, it prohibits arbitrary state classification, discriminatory prosecution, unguided executive discretion, and procedural unfairness.

constitutional_articles.description: The paramount fundamental right guaranteeing life and personal liberty, interpreted judicially to encompass procedural due process, fair trial, speedy trial, dignity, protection against custodial violence, right to legal aid, and victim rights.

supreme_court_cases.case_name: State of Punjab v. Gurmit Singh
supreme_court_cases.summary: Landmark judgment establishing evidentiary guidelines for victim testimony in sexual assault trials.
supreme_court_cases.ratio_decidendi: The sole testimony of a rape victim is reliable and does not require corroboration unless there are compelling reasons to doubt her credibility. Corroboration is not a legal mandate.
supreme_court_cases.holding: Reversed acquittal of accused; laid down guidelines to conduct sexual offence trials in camera and protect victim dignity under Article 21.

supreme_court_cases.case_name: Independent Thought v. Union of India
supreme_court_cases.summary: Landmark ruling striking down Exception 2 to Section 375 IPC, criminalizing sexual intercourse with a minor wife between 15 and 18 years of age.
supreme_court_cases.ratio_decidendi: Bodily integrity, autonomy, and child rights under Articles 14, 15, and 21 paramountly protect minor girls from non-consensual sexual acts, regardless of marital status.
supreme_court_cases.holding: Declared marital rape of minor wives aged 15-18 as an offence under sexual violence penal sections.

supreme_court_cases.case_name: Lalita Kumari v. Government of UP
supreme_court_cases.summary: Landmark Constitution Bench ruling on mandatory registration of FIR upon receipt of cognizable offence information.
supreme_court_cases.ratio_decidendi: Registration of FIR under Section 154 CrPC (now BNSS 173) is mandatory if the information discloses commission of a cognizable offence. Police have no discretion to conduct preliminary inquiry prior to FIR in clear cognizable offences.
supreme_court_cases.holding: Mandated immediate FIR registration for cognizable offences including rape, dowry death, murder, and kidnapping.
